invariants: The text route must be complete without colour, diagram, sound, or gesture.
Adaptation changes communication and logistics, not the urgency threshold.
Use one speaker, one next action, one backup, and one escalation condition.
Ask the person what works; do not infer capacity from speech, movement, eye contact, or distress.

profiles.barrier: Visual-only maps, colour coding, inaccessible exits, or unannounced obstacles
profiles.adaptation: Read the next action aloud; describe direction and obstacles; offer an elbow or requested guiding method; keep mobility aids with the person.
profiles.handoff: State visual access needs, guide method, assistive devices, and whether an accessible route is known.
profiles.failure_escalation: The person cannot leave, orient, or receive critical instructions safely.

profiles.barrier: Voice-only calls, alarms, masks, background noise, or missing text/sign channel
profiles.adaptation: Use text, writing, visual alarms, lip-visible speech when useful, relay/video sign service, or a trusted interpreter chosen by the person.
profiles.handoff: State the preferred language or channel and whether text, sign, lip-reading, or hearing technology is available.
profiles.failure_escalation: Critical instructions or consent cannot be exchanged in time.

profiles.barrier: Speech loss, aphasia, stammering under stress, language mismatch, or a call handler who cannot understand
profiles.adaptation: Use the written emergency card, yes/no questions, pointing, text relay, translation, or a named communication partner without speaking over the person.
profiles.handoff: Show location, problem, danger, callback number, preferred language, and how the person answers yes/no.
profiles.failure_escalation: Location, danger, symptoms, or instructions cannot be communicated.

profiles.barrier: Long explanations, several speakers, figurative language, memory load, or rapidly changing choices
profiles.adaptation: Use literal short sentences; show one action at a time; keep choices binary where possible; repeat the same labels and write the next step down.
profiles.handoff: State that the person needs one speaker, extra processing time, and written or repeated instructions.
profiles.failure_escalation: The person cannot complete the safety action or is becoming more disoriented.

profiles.barrier: Stairs, narrow doors, transfer needs, pain, fatigue, missing equipment, or separation from a mobility aid
profiles.adaptation: Use the accessible route; request trained transfer help; keep wheelchair, walker, prosthesis, charger, and positioning needs with the person.
profiles.handoff: State transfer method, weight-bearing limits, equipment, stair barrier, transport need, and remaining device power.
profiles.failure_escalation: The person cannot leave before the route becomes unsafe or essential positioning/support fails.

profiles.barrier: Bright light, noise, touch, crowding, uncertain social demands, or breathing exercises that intensify distress
profiles.adaptation: Reduce stimulation when safe; ask before touching; offer a non-breath-focused grounding option; use predictable literal language and one contact person.
profiles.handoff: State useful and harmful stimuli, touch preference, communication style, and the person’s established calming or emergency plan.
profiles.failure_escalation: Distress prevents evacuation, communication, essential care, or safe supervision.

minimal_cards.emergency: HELP. LOCATION: ____. DANGER: ____. PERSON AWAKE: YES/NO. BREATHING NORMALLY: YES/NO. CALLBACK: ____.
minimal_cards.safe_place: I have no safe place tonight. I am at ____. I need: shelter / accessible route / power / medication / child safety / violence support / transport.
minimal_cards.communication: I communicate best by: speech / writing / text / sign / pointing / yes-no. Please use one sentence and one question at a time.
